title: Denchūka
description: A summer street in Kyoto, dense with utility poles, run forward through Japan's slow programme of burying its overhead lines. Drag sideways through the years. The wires go first: each one loses its tension, bows, and drops out of the sky. Then the crossarms and transformers are lowered down their poles, and then the poles themselves sink along their own axes into the ground, the far ones first and the big wooden one on the corner last; the one that carries the traffic signal stays for it, stripped bare. The sky behind them is left clean and the street oddly bare and quiet. Drag back and it all comes back the way it went.
intent: Reality pieces: take a real photograph apart element by element and remove each piece together with its effects. Forty-one wires (sky matte with sub-pixel alpha, carried on below the skyline by ridge tracking), the hardware of eight poles (SAM 2.1 masks and contrast detection), and the shafts (SAM 2.1 plus a fitted cylinder) each become their own element; three clean plates are filled (a membrane of the sky round each hole against the sky, LaMa below the skyline, the bare shafts straightened and interpolated along their own length), so every in-between year is two neighbouring clean plates; moving pieces are unmixed against the plate behind them so they carry none of the street. The sun was estimated from the shading across the concrete poles and MoGe-2's gravity and checked against the open pavement: high and to the right, so the poles' shadows fall into kerbs and grass and the photograph carries none that could be lifted. Reference: Japan's Act on the Promotion of Non-Utility-Pole Policies (無電柱化の推進に関する法律, 2016) and the MLIT programme, https://www.mlit.go.jp/road/road/traffic/chicyuka/ ; Japan has more than 35 million poles and still adds about 70,000 a year, https://www.japantimes.co.jp/opinion/2019/10/12/editorials/expedite-burying-power-cables
sources: Photograph: street intersection in Japanese town (Kyoto, Sony a7 II) by Richard Tao (@richardtao28) on Unsplash, Unsplash License. https://unsplash.com/photos/street-intersection-in-japanese-town-jlJFU9QBfFc (file: https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1583200786218-ccee132a8567). Cropped to 3:2 and resampled to 2400x1600. Taken apart by tools/depth/bakes/denchuka (prep.py, masks.py, plates.py, resid.py, membrane.py, shadows.py, export.py) with tools/depth segment.py (SAM 2.1 Hiera-Tiny, Apache-2.0; sky matte), fill.py (LaMa, Apache-2.0) and normals.py (MoGe-2 ViT-S, MIT).
